; the TEI is the witness). Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected; the scans are the witnesses.
scope: The Elements whole in Heiberg's Greek, and the three other works of the Opera omnia that are Euclid's own: the Data, the Optics, and the Phaenomena with the musical writings. The Elements volumes of the Opera omnia (I–V, 1883–88) are the Greek of the TEI and are not doubled here; Heath's English (1908) is a translation and is not seated. The Catoptrica in vol. VII is of doubtful authorship and is seated as Heiberg prints it. The Elements text is 13 books, one line per paragraph of the TEI (definitions, enunciations, proofs), 1.48 million characters.

Elements I, proposition 1 — 'ἐπὶ τῆς δοθείσης εὐθείας πεπερασμένης τρίγωνον ἰσόπλευρον συστήσασθαι.'
Opera omnia VIII, title — 'PHAENOMENA ET SCRIPTA MUSICA'
why_seated: The model of the deductive treatise: definitions, postulates and common notions, and everything after them derived. The archive's own instruments (the operator, the falsification condition, the seat that verifies against its manifest) are written in its debt, and the shelf had no Euclid.
